postTitle: Moving Countries: Rebuilding Your Financial Identity
topic: A transfer app that is cheap on one route can be dear on another, and the cost adds up

cta.subtext: The cheap app depends on the route

caption.instagram:
Your friend's transfer app is cheap. Will it be cheap for your family too?

Not necessarily. What a transfer costs depends on the pair of countries the money travels between. Busy routes with many providers are cheap; thin ones are expensive; the same company can be cheap on one and dear on another.

The cost also has two parts, and only one is advertised: the fee, and the markup built into the exchange rate, which is rarely shown and often the larger part. One comparison captures both: for the same total paid, how much does the person at the other end receive?

It adds up. The World Bank puts the global average cost of a small transfer a little over 6%. At 6.5%, €300 a month costs €2,340 over ten years; at 2%, a competitive provider's price, €720. The €1,620 between them is more than five months of the money itself.
